Urged the Commission to deny the request because she does not want more development in the area and has concerns about how the width of Orchard Avenue would handle a subdivision. With Woodbury 2 nd Addition proposed to the east of Arborcrest Road, the increased traffic would affect the safety of property owners along Orchard Ave. John O’Laughlin, Moscow, was opposed to the proposed development and upset about the current construction traffic along Orchard Ave for the Woodbury development. He requested the City delay approval of the annexation of the subject property until the developers submit their plans for the land. He also expressed concerns about the impact of the Woodbury subdivision on the water from the pump house. Brad Jaeckel, Moscow, spoke in opposition of the proposed rezone and had concerns that the packet information was incorrect regarding the property that was being annexed, as well as the impact to traffic on Orchard Ave. He did not agree that the road is as wide as shared in the staff report and presented. He stated that the subject property is too steep for the density of the proposed zoning district. Mark Solomon, Moscow, was opposed to the proposed rezone and talked about concerns for the water demand of the current residential developable lots already within the City. He stated that the City has gotten too close to the maximum water use recently. Melissa Epler, Moscow, opposed the rezone and urged the Commission to make it Suburban Residential (SR) instead of a R-2 zoning district. She had concerns about the water use within the City without a long-term plan, losing farmland, and too high density for the topography. She also did not think the public hearing notice provided enough time for public input and requested that process be modified. Jason Apt, Moscow, spoke in opposition to the proposed rezone because of the topography of the land. He had concerns about flooding along Orchard Avenue, as well as the current width of Orchard Ave being dangerous for increased traffic users. Scott Becker (applicant’s representative), Moscow, reminded the Commissioners that the proposed rezone and annexation does not include a development project as that has not been planned. Road improvements along Orchard Avenue would be required for future development projects, including the narrow portions of the road to the north. The grade of the property would be partially evened out to accommodate development on the top, as well as to provide access for water and sewer connections. He also mentioned that the Rolling Hills subdivisions are R-2 and have a similar topography. Public Hearing closed at 7:41 PM The Commission talked about what triggers the development and/or expansion of a City street. The current Comprehensive Plan Designation fits a zoning district of R-1, R-2, or R-3 for the subject property. There was continued conversation about the state of Orchard Avenue and the SR zone on the south side of the property. The Commission talked about how the adjacent Orchardview Acres subdivisions were developed. There were concerns about creating more islands of County land within City limits. Scott moved to table the proposed rezone and comprehensive plan designation, seconded by Hamilton. After further discussion about reasons to table the decision, the motion was rescinded by Scott with Hamiltons agreement. The Commission continued to discuss the proposed rezone and comprehensive plan designation. Scott moved to deny the proposed rezone and comp plan designation, stating it does not provide for the logical and orderly location of land uses and lacks a sufficient existing transportation network. The motion was seconded by Hamilton. After further discussion about the reasons to deny the application, the motion was rescinded by Scott with Hamiltons agreement.

Neighborhood Meeting Materials STAFF REVIEW Proposal:  The applicant, Phil Rheingans, is proposing a rezone and Preliminary Subdivision Plat for property generally located east of the current terminus of Third Street near the intersection of Third Street and Mountain View Road within the City of Moscow. The proposal is to rezone a 2.68- acre area which is currently zoned Moderate Density, Single Family Residential (R-2) to the Medium Density Residential (R-3) Zone. The proposed preliminary subdivision plat is a 17.2-acre area to create 64 parcels averaging 9,080 square feet in size, referred to as the Harvest Hills 2  nd Addition. Site and Area Land Use:  The subject property has historically been utilized for agricultural purposes and is currently vacant. The property is adjacent to single family residential developments (Damen’s Addition, Skyview Estates Addition, Moser Estates Addition) to the north, the Rolling Hills Additions to the south, and the Harvest Hills 1 st  Addition directly to the west. Moser Park is directly adjacent to the east and is currently undeveloped. Background:  In 2005, the subject property was annexed into the City and rezoned from Agriculture/Forestry (AF) to the Moderate Density Single Family Residential (R-2) Zoning District. The Comprehensive Plan Land Use Designation at the time was Low Density Residential (LR). Also included in the land use actions in 2005 was a preliminary plat for the Windfall Hills Subdivision. The Windfall Hills Subdivision included 77 single family residential lots, averaging 9,700 sq. ft. at a density of approximately 4.5 units per net acre. The Windfall Hills preliminary plat was approved by City Council on August 1 st , 2005 subject to seven conditions. The developer then submitted a preliminary Planned Unit Development (PUD) to reduce the required front yard setbacks from 25 feet as required by the R-2 Zone to 10 feet. The

2 PUD also included sample home elevations that specified a certain architectural style for the development. In exchange for the reduction in setback requirements, the developer proposed to provide additional landscaping and public amenities above those required by the code, as well as certain design elements of the proposed houses intended to improve the aesthetic appeal of the neighborhood and reduce the amount of site grading. On July 19  th , 2006, the Planning and Zoning Commission approved the preliminary PUD for Windfall Hills with three conditions. On July 21 st, 2008 the Windfall Hills final plat and development agreement came before the City Council and both were subsequently approved. In 2008, the developer of Windfall Hills approached the City about a Verizon pedestal that needed to be moved as part of the proposed subdivision. At the time, the City was contemplating a road improvement project on the portion of Mountain View Road that includes the Windfall Hills Subdivision frontage. There was also a desire by the City to extend the section of Janson Street from the north subdivision plat boundary to its intersection with Damen Street since the development of the Janson Street Extension was not required of the previous subdivision plats to the north. The City and the developer reached an agreement whereas the City would contribute up to $50,000 towards the relocation of the Verizon pedestals and be responsible for the underground utilities on the Janson Street Extension, if the developer paid for public improvements to Mountain View Rd including the bicycle and pedestrian path on the east side and paid for the above-ground improvements  for  the  Janson  Street  Extension.  This  agreement  was  executed  through  a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) which was approved by Council on April 21 st , 2008. Subsequently in 2009 a revised MOU was entered into which replaced the 2008 MOU. Below is a detailed description of what was required within the 2008 MOU and the subsequent 2009 MOU. The 2008 MOU was entered into on July 21 st , 2008 and contained the following requirements of the developer: 1.  That the developer deposit a security for all Mountain View Road bicycle and pedestrian path public improvements by July 27 th , 2008; and 2.  That the developer deposit a security for the above-ground improvements to extend Janson Street from the north subdivision boundary to Damen Street; and 3.  Designating the timing of the aforementioned Janson Street extension to occur in Phase II of the development; and 4.  That the developer dedicate a portion of property for street right-of-way for the widening of Mountain View Road and a 25 ft. wide pedestrian and bicycle path easement to the east of Mountain View Road; and 5.  That the developer assumes the costs in excess of the City’s $50,000 contribution for moving a Verizon pedestal located on the east side of Mountain View Road. The MOU also required that the City: 1.  Assume full financial responsibility up to $50,000 toward the cost of relocation of the Verizon pedestal; and 2.  Assume full financial responsibility for or shall install all required below-ground public improvements for the Janson Street Extension prior to the developer installing all above- ground public improvements required for the Janson Street Extension. For various reasons, portions of the July 21  st , 2008 MOU were not completed and the City and the developer then entered into a June 8 th , 2009 MOU which replaced the previous MOU. The 2009 MOU contained the following requirements of the developer: 1.  That the developer assumes the total cost of the Janson Street Extension prior to receiving building permits on lots within Phase I of the development.

That the developer dedicate a portion of property for street right-of-way for the widening of Mountain View Road and a 25 ft. wide pedestrian and bicycle path easement to the east of Mountain View Road on or before June 3, 2009; and 3.  That the developer shall grant a 35 ft. wide easement for street purposes on the east side of Mountain View Road for the widening of the road; and 4.  That the developer shall file the final plat for Windfall Hills Subdivision by June 3 rd , 2009. The 2009 MOU required that the City: 1.  Construct improvements on Mountain View Road including paving, curb and gutter, and a drainage system; and 2.  The aforementioned improvements shall include the entire subdivision frontage as well as the Hoffman unplatted property to the south of the subdivision. The City has since constructed the agreed-upon construction improvements on Mountain View Road and the developer only completed conditions #2 and #3 that were required above. The developer failed to record the final plat for the Windfall Hills Subdivision so consequently the Windfall Hills Subdivision final plat approval expired and the Janson Street Extension was never paid for or completed. In 2013, a preliminary subdivision plat on the subject property was approved for Harvest Hills Addition that was very similar to the original Windfall Hills proposal. There were five conditions placed upon the approval which included the requirement that the applicant construct Janson Street and that a portion of Third Street be widened to accommodate on-street parking on one side of the street. After the preliminary plat approval the applicant indicated that the approved project was not financially feasible and never proceeded with the final plat stage of the subdivision plat process. Then in 2015, the applicant submitted a new Harvest Hills subdivision plat for only 7.45 acres of the entire 24.7-acre property. The applicant proposed to rezone the majority of the property to Medium Density Single Family Residential (R-3) and plat twinhomes lots and also create a 2.2- acre Neighborhood Business (NB) lot at the intersection of Mountain View Road and Third Street. On February 1, 2016, City Council approved the proposed rezone request and then on April 18, 2016 the Council approved the preliminary subdivision plat for Harvest Hills 1  st  Addition with three conditions. Since the proposed subdivision plat boundary did not extend to the Janson Street intersection, the Council approved a new MOU and Development Agreement that allowed the deferral of the construction of Janson Street to future plats to the east. In 2021, the applicant then submitted a preliminary subdivision plat for the remaining 17.2-acre area of land located directly east of the Harvest Hills 1  st  Addition and referred to as Harvest Hills 2  nd  Addition. The proposal included 56 lots ranging from 7,219 to 24,075 square feet in size and was approved by City Council on September 7, 2021. The applicant then failed to submit the final plat documents to the Latah County Recorder’s Office within 180 days of Council approval, so the 2021 approval was rendered null and void.

7 Zoning:  The subject property is currently designated as the Moderate Density Residential (R-2) Zoning District. The properties to the north, east, and south of the subject property are also zoned R-2. Harvest Hills 1 st  Addition to the west is zoned a combination of the Neighborhood Business (NB) and Medium Density Residential (R-3) Zones. The applicant is proposing to rezone a 2.68- acre area which is currently zoned Moderate Density, Single Family Residential (R-2) to the Medium Density Residential (R-3) Zone. The R-2 zoning district is a moderate density residential zone appropriate where the following circumstances are present: 1.  Single family dwellings predominate. 2.  The terrain is not harshly irregular and smaller lot sizes can be accommodated without extensive earthwork. 3.  Utilities and other public facilities are adequate for the densities allowed. 4.  Existing lot development patterns and policies embodied in the Plan will also guide application of this zoning district. Uses permitted within the R-2 Zone include single-family residential dwellings, market and community gardens, group child care facilities, and public parks and recreational facilities. The Medium Density Residential (R-3) Zoning District provides for an increase over the density allowed by the R-2 zoning district by permitting different types of housing construction. It is appropriate where activity levels are moderate, terrain permits construction of somewhat larger structures, and where public systems and neighborhood facilities can accommodate a greater intensity of land use as guided by the Comprehensive Plan. Uses permitted within the R-3 Zone include single-family dwellings, two family dwellings, twinhomes, townhouses, market and community gardens, group and small child care facilities, and public parks and recreation facilities.

9 Preliminary Plat:  The applicant is proposing to subdivide the existing 17.2-acre area to create 64 parcels averaging 9,080 square feet in size, referred to as the Harvest Hills 2  nd  Addition. There are 18 twinhome lots which are proposed within the R-3 portion of the subdivision and 46 standard single-family lots within the R-2 portion. The minimum lot size within the R-2 Zone is 7,000 sf and minimum lot width of 60 feet. The minimum lot size for twinhomes within the R-3 Zone is 3,250 square feet and the minimum lot width is 30 feet. All proposed lots meet the minimum lot size and width requirements for their respective zones. Water and Sewer:  Water service is proposed to be extended via existing water mains that have been extended to the current terminus of Third Street at the far east end of Harvest Hills 1  st  Addition. A new water main will be extended off of the existing and will extend along the Third Street alignment to the eastern subdivision boundary. Sanitary sewer currently exists within the Third Street alignment on the subject property and is currently connected to Rolling Hills 8 th  Addition. This 8” sanitary sewer main was installed previously as part of an agreement between the previous Windfall Hills developer and the developer of the Rolling Hills Additions. Sanitary sewer mains will be extended through Janson Street and Amber Court to the eastern subdivision boundary. Storm Sewer will be conveyed through the subdivision through a new main in Third Street that connects with the main in Harvest Hills 1 st  Addition and the storm main extending from Rolling Hills 8 th  Addition. The stormwater will ultimately be conveyed to stormwater detention ponds in Harvest Hills 1 st  Addition. The stormwater detention ponds then drain to Paradise Creek. Access, Streets, Traffic:  The subject property is located adjacent to Third Street to the west which is designated as a collector street. The section of Third Street adjacent to the subject property is developed as a 34-foot-wide roadway with two travel lanes, bike lanes on both sides of the street, and curbing and gutters on both sides of the street. A portion of the north side of Third Street within Harvest Hills 1 st  Addition is widened to provide nine (9) on-street parking spaces per a City Council condition for the Harvest Hills 1 st  Addition plat. The proposed preliminary plat includes the continuation of Third Street to the east. Third Street through the subject property is also considered a collector street and will be developed to the same standard as Harvest Hills 1  st  Addition, with bike lanes and no on-street parking permitted. There are two pedestrian pathway connections provided on the preliminary plat. At the far east end of the development there is a right-of-way dedication that provides a ten-foot-wide connection from Amber Court to Moser Park. Additionally, between Lots 8 and 9 of Block 4 there is a proposed ten- foot-wide pedestrian easement which allows for the connection of the pedestrian pathway which extends to the property from Third Street to the south. Parkland Dedication:  The subject property contains approximately 13.32 acres of net developable land. The developer is required to dedicate 5% of the net developable land within the R-2 Zone and 7% within the R-3 Zone. The total parkland dedication requirement for Harvest Hills 2  nd  Addition is 32,876 square feet. There is an excess balance of 11,265 square feet that was dedicated and

10 banked as part of Harvest Hills 1 st  Addition, which results in a total parkland dedication requirement of 21,611 square feet. The developer has proposed a 19,083 square foot island at the center of the cul-de-sac and a 10-foot-wide, 1,525 square foot tract that provides pedestrian access from Amber Court to Moser Park. The sum of the two proposed dedications is 1,003 square feet short of the total parkland dedication requirement of the proposed subdivision and the Parks and Recreation Department has recommended that the developer pay a fee in lieu of dedication for the remaining parkland.
